questions.q: What is the article's central point?
options: Setbacks should be avoided at all costs
Big breakthroughs matter more than daily habits
Small improvements compound into large results over time
Cycling success depends on equipment alone
questions.explain: The article argues that aggregating 1 percent gains yields remarkable results.

questions.q: What did the team do to the inside of the team truck?
options: Painted it white to spot dust
questions.explain: They painted it white so dust that could harm the bikes would be noticed.

questions.q: Who was the first British cyclist to win the Tour de France?
questions.explain: Bradley Wiggins won in 2012, with Froome winning the next year.

questions.q: If you improve 1 percent daily for a year, how much better are you?
questions.explain: The article says you'd end up thirty-seven times better.

questions.q: What does the author imply about habits and goals?
options: Systems matter more than specific goals
Only elite athletes benefit from marginal gains
questions.explain: He says the system is greater than the goal and mastering habits matters more than a given outcome.
